title: Baby Geese Jump Off a 400-Foot Cliff Within a Day of Hatching

scenes.text: Baby geese jump off a four-hundred-foot cliff.
They do it when they're about a day old.
Barnacle geese nest on cliff ledges to stay away from foxes.
But the grass and water the chicks need are at the bottom.
So their parents call from below, and the chicks leap.
Their bones are still soft, and they're light and fluffy.
About nine in ten survive the fall.
Four hundred feet. One day old. Watch it again.

description:
Baby geese jump off a four-hundred-foot cliff when they are about a day old.
Barnacle goose chicks leap from cliff nests to reach food below, and about nine in ten survive the fall.
Could you take that leap?
first_comment: Bonus: only about half of the chicks live to become young adults, mostly because of predators. Which part of their life is harder?
